title: Generic stabilization by static output feedback
decision_reason: Explicit primary question, independent specialist restatement, live status and resolution-scope checks, mathematical duplicate review and separated A31 self-pass passed.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Real continuous-time LTI triples (A,B,C); constant real gain K; closed loop A+BKC
problem_fingerprint.dimension: A n×n, B n×m, C p×n, K m×p; n=mp
problem_fingerprint.domain: All real matrix triples with usual Euclidean topology
problem_fingerprint.regularity_and_data_class: Constant finite-dimensional real matrices without structural constraints
problem_fingerprint.boundary_or_initial_conditions: Strict Hurwitz spectrum ensures asymptotic stability for every initial state
problem_fingerprint.parameter_range: Positive integer m,p; all real gains allowed
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: Classify m,p such that an open dense set of plants each admits some K; gain depends on plant
problem_fingerprint.limit_regime_and_order: Genericity over all triples for each pair; no random-plant law
problem_fingerprint.requested_conclusion: Exact dimension criterion for density of stabilizable triples
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: Not a decidability problem; real-algebraic decision procedures already exist in principle

statement_source_and_scope_match: E10 p. 2 Question; BA84 §2 Question 2 at critical n=mp; EG02 Euclidean generic convention. Inputs/outputs swapped relative to E10 notation only. Stabilizable locus is open. Algebraic genericity agrees here because the locus is semialgebraic; this equivalence is an inference from the polynomial Hurwitz formulation, not an additional conjecture.
proposed_statement_text: For n=mp, determine all positive integer pairs (m,p) for which {(A,B,C): there is a real constant K with A+BKC Hurwitz} is dense in R^(n×n)×R^(n×m)×R^(p×n).
applied_significance: Fundamental sufficiency of actuator/sensor counts for memoryless measured-output stabilization; no numerical linear algebra problem or universal robust design claim.
